page: Microsoft Azure D96s_v6 is a general purpose virtual machine instance running on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. It is provisioned with 48 physical cores across 96 dedicated vCPUs with hyper-threading enabled, accompanied by 384.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio (4.0 GB per vCPU). The CPU features a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache, alongside hardware instruction support for AVX-512, AMX (tile and int8), and advanced cryptographic extensions including AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance contains no bundled local storage (None) and no dedicated GPUs.

Benchmark testing indicates exceptionally strong parallel processing capabilities. The instance scored 85,698.46 in the PassMark CPU suite and achieved 81,378.95 in stress-ng multi-core testing, placing it in the upper percentiles for multi-threaded computation. Extended instruction tests reached 106,181.55, reflecting the presence of hardware acceleration flags like AMX and AVX-512. Software compilation with Clang achieved 52,570.0 and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression delivered 460.38 GB/sec. Conversely, single-core benchmarks remain balanced within the median range, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1,948.29 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1,850.0.

Data serving and caching performance remain high, highlighted by 105.25 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks, 114.52 GB/sec in static web serving, and a 25,128.71 rating in PassMark database operations. Small cached read bandwidth registers at 6,201.91 GB/sec, though uncached large-block transfers drop to 148.49 GB/sec for reads and 69.02 GB/sec for writes, resulting in a lower relative PassMark memory rating. CPU-based LLM inference shows viable throughput, maintaining 254.86 prompt tokens/sec and 29.53 generation tokens/sec on 7B models.

Architecturally, the absence of bundled local disks requires reliance on external remote storage, which represents a primary design tradeoff. Given its massive core count, high network and caching metrics, and standard memory density, Microsoft Azure D96s_v6 provides solid compute efficiency for distributed microservices, CI/CD compilation pipelines, high-concurrency web serving, and in-memory key-value stores.

Providing 96 dedicated vCPUs across 48 physical cores and 384.0 GB of RAM, it maintains a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio alongside a 260 MB L3 cache and advanced vector and matrix extensions (AVX-512, AMX). The server includes no GPUs and relies strictly on external remote storage, featuring no bundled local disks. Benchmark evaluations show top-tier multi-threaded processing, static web serving throughput of 114.52 GB/sec, and 105.25 million operations per second in Redis SET tests, contrasted with average single-core output. D96s_v6 is technically suited for multi-threaded compilation, high-traffic web infrastructure, distributed caching, and large enterprise applications.
